predecessors.name: Kingdom of Mapungubwe
predecessors.text: 'In the 13th century Great Zimbabwe was on the fringe of the Mapungubwe state'; 'Around 1300, Great Zimbabwe replaced Mapungubwe as the most important trading centre in the interior'

successors.name: Kingdom of Butua
successors.text: 'The state was composed of over 150 smaller zimbabwes, and likely covered 50,000 km2' (a 126 km disc around Great Zimbabwe has the same area)

ledger.x: c. 1250: Great Zimbabwe, a Shona stone-built capital, is a leading trade centre of the plateau. 'By 1250 Great Zimbabwe had become an important trade centre'; the infobox says 'Established: 13th century' and the page gives no single founding year or founder.

c. 1450: the Great Zimbabwe core passes to the Butua kingdom as the capital is deserted. certainty.note: No frontier is described; the realm was a tributary and trade network of over 150 smaller zimbabwes.
